items.title: Library supplement: Finite Gaussian Hermite Gram formula

source.anchor: F6 in source-only.json; proof topology P4.
source.attribution: Original generic exposition of Gaussian polynomial and finite Hermite features; existing proofs reused without a novelty or primary-textbook completion claim.

items.statement: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel structure, and let \(\gamma_E=\operatorname{stdGaussian}(E)\) be the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability. Let \(H_j\) be the unnormalized probabilists Hermite polynomial and put \(h_j(w)=[x\mapsto H_j(\langle w,x\rangle)]\in L^2(\gamma_E)\). For a finite set \(S\subset\mathbb N\) and real coefficients \(c_j\), put \(F_{S,c}(w)=\sum_{j\in S}c_jh_j(w)\). For every finite \(S\), arbitrary real \(c_j\), and actual unit vectors \(w,z\), the Hilbert inner product is the following diagonal sum. Signed correlations, both endpoint correlations, degree zero and empty support are included.
assumptions: The finite-dimensional real inner-product and Borel structures are the actual structures on the same carrier \(E\).
\(\gamma_E\) is the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability. No positive dimension restriction is imposed.
Both directions satisfy \(\|w\|=\|z\|=1\). They need not be independent or orthogonal.
\(S\) and the real coefficients are arbitrary; no parity, positivity, or total-mass normalization is imposed.

bindings.boundary: These are finite polynomial and actual Gaussian Hilbert-space results. Infinite-series limits and application-specific force identities require separate proofs.

The correlation may be negative or equal to either endpoint; degree zero and empty S are included. Both directions must be unit; no independence is assumed.
